items.t: Walmex stock weighs digital growth against Q3 margin pressure
sum: Walmart de México y Centroamérica delivered stronger sales but weaker earnings in the July-to-September quarter, according to ESM Magazine. The report, published on November 2, said consolidated revenue rose 3.0% year over year to MXN 248.8 billion, while constant-currency growth reached 3.6%.

Mexico revenue increased 3.1% to MXN 206.7 billion, while Central America grew 6.0% to MXN 42.1 billion. Mexico e-commerce net sales advanced 15.8%, supported by a 20.8% increase in store-fulfilled sales.

Consolidated EBITDA rose 0.4% to MXN 25.4 billion, but the EBITDA margin narrowed by 30 basis points to 10.2%. Quarterly net profit stood at MXN 11.0 billion, leaving the retailer with sales momentum but limited earnings conversion.

Management said it was encouraged by the early signs but not satisfied with the breadth of performance. The next phase will depend on whether digital expansion, price investments and productivity measures can improve operating leverage.
Walmex stock traded at 2.64 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:05 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026.

Compared with the 2.55-euro quote in the previous report published on Thursday, November 5, at 16:37 CET, the quote was 3.53% higher. This comparison is measured against the previous report, not against a same-session Xetra close. The real-time quote of Walmex stock is available separately.

For investors, the central issue remains the balance between digital reach and margin recovery. The unchanged outlook keeps execution, cost control and productivity at the center of the next reporting cycle.

items.t: Walmex stock balances digital growth against weaker Q3 profit
sum: Walmart de México y Centroamérica increased third-quarter revenue, but investment and operating costs continued to weigh on earnings. ESM Magazine reported on November 2 that revenue for the July-September period rose 3.0 percent year over year to MXN 248.8 billion, or 3.6 percent in constant currency.

Mexico revenue grew 3.1 percent to MXN 206.7 billion, while Central America advanced 6.0 percent to MXN 42.1 billion. Same-store sales increased 1.7 percent in Mexico and 4.8 percent in Central America, with the Mexican average ticket up 1.6 percent while traffic remained broadly flat.

Digital commerce provided the clearest growth support. Mexico e-commerce net sales climbed 15.8 percent, and store-fulfilled sales increased 20.8 percent. The figures point to stronger digital reach beyond physical-store traffic, although the expansion requires continued spending on technology, capacity and price competitiveness.

ESM Magazine reported that consolidated EBITDA rose 0.4 percent to MXN 25.4 billion, while the EBITDA margin contracted 30 basis points to 10.2 percent. Quarterly net profit was MXN 11.0 billion, leaving profitability behind the pace of digital expansion.

Management reaffirmed its 2026 outlook for consolidated sales growth of 3.5 percent to 4.5 percent in constant currency. It also continued to expect the EBITDA margin to finish slightly below the prior year's level. For investors, execution and productivity remain central because the current growth strategy is generating sales momentum before fully converting that momentum into profit.

Walmex stock traded at 2.55 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 16:37 CET on Thursday, November 5, 2026. The new quote was 1.19 percent away from the 2.52-euro quote in the previous report published at 15:11 CET on the same day.
The real-time quote of Walmex stock provides the latest trading indication for investors following the balance between growth and margins.

items.t: Walmex stock trades at 2.49 euros after margin pressure report
sum: Walmart de México y Centroamérica's third-quarter results left the retailer balancing sales expansion against higher operating costs. Reuters reported on October 27 that net profit fell 6 percent year over year to MXN 11.03 billion for the July-September period, while revenue rose 3 percent to MXN 248.83 billion.

Walmex stock traded at 2.49 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:42 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. That compares with 2.44 euros in the latest relevant own report at 17:12 CET on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, an increase of 2.05 percent since that report. This comparison is separate from a daily Xetra close comparison.

The quarterly pressure was concentrated in profitability. EBITDA increased only 0.4 percent to MXN 25.37 billion, while the EBITDA margin narrowed by 30 basis points to 10.2 percent. Operating profit fell 1.8 percent to MXN 18.68 billion as expenses rose faster than sales.

Digital commerce provided a counterweight. According to Reuters, online gross merchandise value increased 15 percent in Mexico and 23 percent in Central America. Mexico same-store sales rose almost 2 percent, helped by a 1.6 percent increase in the average ticket, while customer traffic was broadly flat.

Management reaffirmed its 2026 forecast for consolidated sales growth of 3.5 percent to 4.5 percent in constant currency. It expects the EBITDA margin to finish slightly below the prior year's level, keeping margin execution central to the investment case.

Walmex opened 42 stores during the quarter, including 39 in Mexico and three in Central America. The expansion increases the retailer's growth base but also raises the spending burden that investors will monitor in coming quarters. The company's official website lists the third-quarter 2026 results release dated October 27.

items.t: Walmex stock faces margin pressure as digital sales accelerate
Walmex stock posts Q3 profit drop as digital sales accelerate
sum: Walmart de México y Centroamérica reported third-quarter results on October 27, 2026, showing continued digital momentum but weaker profitability. According to Morningstar, citing Dow Jones, revenue rose 3.0% year over year to MXN 248.83 billion in the July-September quarter, while net profit declined 6.1% to MXN 11.03 billion.

Expense growth outpaced sales growth. General expenses increased 5.7% and reached 17.4% of sales, compared with 17.0% a year earlier. Walmex said the increase largely reflected investments in new stores, e-commerce, technology and staffing, partly offset by productivity and efficiency measures.

Operating profit fell 1.8% to MXN 18.68 billion, while EBITDA edged up 0.4% to MXN 25.37 billion. The resulting pressure reduced the EBITDA margin by 30 basis points to 10.2%, highlighting the near-term cost of the retailer's expansion and digital investment program.

Digital channels remained a key counterweight. E-commerce sales in Mexico increased 16%, while goods delivered from stores rose 21%. In Mexico, same-store sales gained 1.7%, supported by a 1.6% increase in the average ticket, while customer traffic was little changed. Central American same-store sales rose 4.8%.

Management reaffirmed its 2026 forecast for consolidated sales growth of 3.5% to 4.5% in constant currency. The company expects the EBITDA margin to finish slightly below the prior year's level. For investors, the unchanged outlook indicates that management is maintaining its growth plan despite the quarterly earnings decline, while margin performance remains the central near-term issue.

Walmex opened 42 stores during the quarter, including 39 in Mexico and three in Central America. The expansion adds to the investment base that is supporting future sales but also contributes to the expense pressure visible in the latest results.
Walmex stock traded at 2.41 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 12:27 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Walmex stock.

items.t: Walmart+ lands in Mexico at MXN 89 a month, its second market outside the US
sum: Walmart launched its Walmart+ paid membership in Mexico on October 29, 2026, pricing it at MXN 89 a month or MXN 890 a year and folding shipping, a streaming service, mobile data, a health program and doubled rewards into a single subscription, according to an announcement Walmart published from Mexico City. Mexico is the second country outside the United States to receive the program, following Canada in June.

Walmart now sells a monthly membership in Mexico that gives people cheaper or free delivery, a TV streaming service, extra phone data and health discounts for one fee. It matters because a paid membership tells Walmart exactly who its most frequent customers are, and that kind of knowledge is what retail advertising businesses are built on. Shoppers in Mexico now have a membership at MXN 89 a month to weigh up, but the company has not said what happens to the older Walmart Pass membership it sold before.

The membership is operated by Walmart de México y Centroamérica, the listed subsidiary known as Walmex, and its components draw heavily on businesses that subsidiary already runs. According to Walmart, members receive six groups of benefits.

Delivery is the core of the offer. According to Walmart, members get free delivery on scheduled orders of MXN 399 or more. As an introductory benefit through November 30, 2026, that minimum is waived, so scheduled orders of any size qualify for free delivery until the end of November.

Shipping is where the announcement contradicts itself. Its first benefit line says members "enjoy free shipping with no minimum purchase." Its second line, under the heading "Unlimited shipping," says members get free shipping "on eligible purchases of MXN $399 or more through Walmart's digital channels," and adds that "as an introductory benefit through November 30, 2026, free shipping will also be available with no minimum purchase requirement." Both cannot describe the standard terms. Walmart de México's own Walmart+ sign-up page settles the matter in favor of the second version: it advertises unlimited free shipping on online purchases from MXN 399 at Walmart and Walmart Express. On that reading, the no-minimum offer is a promotion that expires after November 30, and the free shipping threshold for members then returns to MXN 399.

Walmex stock faces profit pressure despite digital growth
sum: Walmart de Mexico y Centroamerica reported weaker profitability for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, as higher expenses and taxes outweighed continued sales and digital-commerce growth. The company released the results on Tuesday, October 27, according to Morningstar.

Net profit declined 6.1 percent year over year to MXN 11.03 billion from MXN 11.75 billion. Earnings per share decreased to MXN 0.642 from MXN 0.678. Consolidated revenue rose 3 percent to MXN 248.83 billion, but the increase remained below the pace of operating-cost growth.

General expenses increased 5.7 percent in reported terms and 6.3 percent in constant currency. They reached 17.4 percent of sales, compared with 17 percent a year earlier. Operating profit fell 1.8 percent to MXN 18.68 billion, while EBITDA edged up 0.4 percent to MXN 25.37 billion.

The higher spending reflected investments in new stores, e-commerce, technology and staffing. Management also pointed to a higher effective tax rate caused by non-recurring adjustments related to prior-year tax calculations. The company expects that rate to normalize in the fourth quarter, according to an Investing.com transcript.

Mexico same-store sales increased 1.7 percent, with the average ticket up 1.6 percent while customer traffic was broadly unchanged. Central American same-store sales rose 4.8 percent, supported by higher customer numbers and a larger average basket.

E-commerce provided stronger momentum. Mexico digital net sales increased 16 percent, including 21 percent growth in store-fulfilled deliveries. Across the group, revenue advanced 3.6 percent in constant currency, compared with 3 percent on a reported basis. The combination of market-share gains and digital expansion supports Walmex's longer-term growth strategy, but the quarter also showed the near-term cost of maintaining price competitiveness and investing in capacity.

Management reaffirmed its 2026 guidance for consolidated sales growth of 3.5 to 4.5 percent in constant currency. It continues to expect the EBITDA margin to finish slightly below the prior year's level of 10.2 percent. For investors, the central issue is whether digital growth and productivity improvements can offset continued pressure from pricing investments, store expansion and labor costs.

Why Is Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) in the Spotlight as Its Holiday Plans Take Shape?
sum: - Walmart announced holiday shopping initiatives for the twenty twenty-six season, covering savings events and faster delivery.
- The retailer is widely read as a barometer for American household spending as the holiday weeks begin.
- Advertising, marketplace and membership are higher-margin businesses growing on top of store traffic.

Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) Consumer Defensive Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) 127.69 USD +4.180 3.384% Last Updated at: 2026-11-02T21:03:00Z , a member of the S&P 500, is stepping into the busiest stretch of the retail year with a fresh round of holiday shopping announcements. Coverage published this autumn describes new holiday shopping initiatives from the Arkansas-based retailer for the twenty twenty-six season, including savings events, faster delivery and expanded ways to shop. This explainer was written on October twenty-ninth and relies on the references listed at the end. It keeps financial detail qualitative where a figure could not be verified, and it does not claim that the holiday push is a result or a guidance change. It is a seasonal business update, and readers should treat it that way. This report is part of our Bluechip Stocks coverage.

For the largest retailer in the world by revenue, the weeks between late October and the end of December carry outsized weight. Households decide where to spend gift budgets, and stores and websites compete on price, assortment and speed. Walmart's announcements ahead of the season typically describe the timing of its deal events, the use of its mobile app, pickup and delivery options, and the way artificial intelligence tools are helping shoppers find products.
How Is Walmart Inc. Organized and Where Does It Earn Its Money?

Walmart reports three main segments. Walmart United States is by far the largest, built around supercenters, neighborhood markets and its online store, and it leans heavily on groceries, which draw frequent visits. Walmart International includes Walmart de Mexico and Central America, Canada, and Flipkart in India, along with operations in other regions. Sam's Club is the membership warehouse chain, competing with Costco and BJ's Wholesale.
